# Reglet

> .NET 10 library that creates, reads and converts DOCX, ODT, PDF and HTML documents from one format-neutral model, with no dependencies beyond the base class library.

- Install: `dotnet add package Reglet` (facade). `Reglet.Core`, `Reglet.Docx`, `Reglet.Odt`, `Reglet.Pdf`, `Reglet.Html`, `Reglet.Fonts` and `Reglet.Hyphenation` can be used on their own.
- Build a document with `PortableDocument.Create()`, write it with `DocumentWriter.WriteAsync(document, "out.pdf")` (format from the extension), read one with `DocumentReader`.
- Documents are immutable; all lengths are stored in points (`Length`).
- Unicode text in PDF needs caller-provided TrueType fonts (`PdfWriteOptions.FontCollection`).
- Drawn pages (data sheets, labels): `PdfCanvas` draws text, lines, rectangles and images at fixed coordinates (points, origin top left, y down); `MeasureText` returns the drawn width.
- Migrating from MigraDoc: fields and empty paragraphs take their paragraph's font size; `ImageBlock.TakesAnchorLine = false` floats an image without an empty anchor line; `TableBlock.CellPaddingHorizontal`/`CellPaddingVertical` and `LeftIndent` give MigraDoc's 1.2 mm side padding with the text at the margin.
- A preview that looks like the PDF: `PdfDocumentWriter.WriteHtmlAsync` (or `PdfCanvas.WriteHtmlAsync`) writes the PDF's pages as HTML; `PdfHtmlOptions` selects a full document or a fragment with a class prefix. The flow HTML of `DocumentWriter` with `.html` is simple and editable, not page-faithful.
